what: The pipeline configuration whose held-out results become the README headline figures (evals/HELDOUT_PROTOCOL.md 6a).
why: Two changes under ledgerql/ after H1, declared together as one configuration before any held-out run (no held-out question exists yet). (1) ledgerql/verify.py: the independent audit (reports/number_audit_vs_verify.md) found the verifier refused true statements ($416B, 416 bn, $0.4T, FY25, 3rd) and accepted invented ones (a figure inside its flat 1% tolerance, every spelled-out number, a form-code lookalike such as 391-K). It now reads magnitude abbreviations, spelled-out numbers, FY labels, dates and period labels, and a stated figure must agree to the precision it states (a round number is read as a rounding only when hedged). (2) ledgerql/pipeline.py: the text of a draft the verifier blocks is stored (blocked_draft, blocked_claims), so the auditor can judge each block as an invented number or a verifier false positive; without it figure 1a counts blocks, not inventions. Neither change touches generation, the vote, the guardrails, the framing or the linker.

amended.what: A whole number with trailing zeros passes as a rounding to its last non-zero place only when the answer hedges the figure (about, approximately, roughly, around, nearly, ~); unhedged trailing zeros are stated digits. The same day, in the auditor and the protocol (not under ledgerql/): a year or date the database holds only for a different company is ungrounded, not weak, and weak is coarse rounding only.
amended.why: Unhedged, the trailing-zero reading reintroduces most of the flat 1% tolerance by another route. Another company's period on this company's figure is the misattributed-period error the year rule exists to catch.
amended.why_an_amendment_and_not_H3: Nothing was run under H2 as first declared: no held-out question exists, the declaring commit was never pushed, and the only execution of that code was 4 of 103 dev cases of a local 7B run that was abandoned without a report (MJ, 2026-10-03).

changes_from_H1: ledgerql/verify.py: precision-aware number verifier (no flat 1% tolerance); magnitude abbreviations; spelled-out numbers; FY labels as years; dates and Q/H labels as claims; fixed list of SEC form codes; the row count grounds a plain count; a ratio cell grounds a percentage; a trailing-zero rounding passes only with a hedge word
ledgerql/pipeline.py: a blocked draft's text and refused claims are stored in the result and the audit log
